messages.author: 299a5089d6c6c523
messages.subject: Re: Problem to deploy my first shiny app
parts:
My apologies, we rolled out a change yesterday intended to make the error one receives when there is an issue with determining Bioconductor packages *more* informative, and ended up making it less so.

The fix for the less informative message should roll out this afternoon.

The underlying problem is that the rsconnect (and its use of packrat) was unable to determine the repository for your Bioconductor packages. We aren't entirely certain the circumstances under which this happens, but typically folks install the latest BiocInstaller and reinstall the Bioconductor packages.

messages.subject: Re: Problem to deploy my first shiny app
parts:
I have updated all the bioconductor packages and I launched the "biocLite("BiocUpgrade")" command, but I got the same error.

Here the packages that I load in ui.R and server.R :

list.of.packages <- c("shiny", "shinythemes", "shinyjs", "DT", "ggplot2","data.table","devtools","RColorBrewer")
new.packages <- list.of.packages[!(list.of.packages %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if(length(new.packages)) install.packages(new.packages, repos='http://cran.us.r-project.org')


source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
list.of.packages <- c("DESeq2", "rtracklayer")
new.packages <- list.of.packages[!(list.of.packages %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if(length(new.packages)) biocLite(new.packages)


list.of.packages <- c("plotly")
new.packages <- list.of.packages[!(list.of.packages %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if(length(new.packages)) devtools::install_github("ropensci/plotly")


list.of.packages <- c("heatmaply")
new.packages <- list.of.packages[!(list.of.packages %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if(length(new.packages))devtools::install_github('talgalili/heatmaply')




library("plotly")
library("shiny")
library("shinythemes")
library("shinyjs")
library("DT")
library("ggplot2")
library("DESeq2")
library("rtracklayer")
library("data.table")
library("heatmaply")
library("RColorBrewer")

The fix for the less informative message should roll out this afternoon.

The underlying problem is that the rsconnect (and its use of packrat) was unable to determine the repository for your Bioconductor packages. We aren't entirely certain the circumstances under which this happens, but typically folks install the latest BiocInstaller and reinstall the Bioconductor packages.

http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/getting-started.html#using-your-r-packages-in-the-cloud
